Predict method for rrGDM models

Source: R/predict.R
predict.rrGDM.Rd

Obtains predictions from a fitted rrGDM object. This method can either project new environmental data into the latent ordination space or calculate pairwise dissimilarities between sites. It supports parametric bootstrapping to assess parameter uncertainty and site-level dispersion.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rrGDM'
predict(
  object,
  newdata = NULL,
  boot = TRUE,
  sample_param = TRUE,
  n_sim = 1000,
  sim_site = TRUE,
  ordination = FALSE,
  type = c("response", "link"),
  probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
  conditional = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An object of class rrGDM.

newdata

A data frame containing new environmental predictor values. If NULL, predictions are made for the original data used in model fitting.

boot

Logical. Should predictions account for parameter and site-level uncertainty via simulation? Defaults to TRUE. If FALSE, a single prediction is returned and sample_param, sim_site, n_sim and probs are ignored.

sample_param

Logical. If TRUE, parameters (lambda and beta) are sampled from the variance-covariance matrix. This requires standard errors (fit the model with se = TRUE or run include_se). Defaults to TRUE.

n_sim

Integer specifying the number of simulation draws. Defaults to 1000.

sim_site

Logical. Should site-level random variation be included in the predictions? Defaults to TRUE.

ordination

Logical. If TRUE, returns coordinates in the latent space. If FALSE, returns pairwise dissimilarities. Defaults to FALSE.

type

Character string; "response" returns dissimilarities on the observed scale (e.g., 0-1), while "link" returns Euclidean distances in the latent space. Defaults to "response".

probs

Numeric vector of probabilities for calculating quantiles from the simulated distribution. Defaults to c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975).

conditional

Logical. If TRUE, returns predictions from the fitted (conditional) latent positions of the samples used to fit the model, including sample-level and random-effect deviations. Only available when newdata = NULL. Sets boot = FALSE. Defaults to FALSE.

...

Ignored.

Value

A data.frame. If ordination = TRUE: the latent coordinates (columns L.1, ..., L.k), the sample number (sample) and the columns of newdata. With boot = TRUE there is one row per sample and draw, and a column draw. If ordination = FALSE: one row per pair of rows of newdata, with the row numbers of the pair (s1, s2) and either the predicted dissimilarity (dist, if boot = FALSE) or one column per value of probs (named "2.5%", "50%", ..., if boot = TRUE).

Details

Simulations (boot = TRUE) use R's random number generator: call set.seed() beforehand for reproducible results.

Examples

set.seed(2)
# simulate data
n <- 25 # sites
p <- 25 # species

env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n))
eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)
Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p,
            dimnames = list(paste0("site", 1:n), paste0("sp", 1:p)))

fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,
             formula = ~ temp + moist,
             family = "binomial")
#> ℹ Preparing data
#> ✔ Preparing data ... done
#> 
#> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA)
#> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done
#> 
#> ℹ optimisation
#> ℹ Start 1/1: objective = 1670.1661
#> ℹ optimisation

#> ✔ optimisation ... done
#> 
#  predict
pred <- predict(fit, boot = FALSE) # point predictions, all pairs
#> ℹ Returning dissimilarities as distances between centroids.
#> ! Note: Distances between centroids are not equivalent to the expected
#>   (average) distances or dissimilarities between samples, which can be much
#>   larger.
#> • To calculate expected dissimilarities between samples, set `boot = TRUE` and
#>   `sim_site = TRUE`.
head(pred)
#>   s1 s2      dist
#> 1  1  2 0.8835308
#> 2  1  3 0.8790634
#> 3  1  4 0.8763481
#> 4  1  5 0.8586837
#> 5  1  6 0.8996577
#> 6  1  7 0.8921820

# Predict ordination coordinates
pred_ord <- predict(fit,
                    ordination = TRUE, # latent positions
                    conditional = TRUE)

head(pred_ord)
#>           L.1        L.2 sample        temp      moist
#> 1 -0.80450922 -1.6343846      1 -0.89691455 -2.4517064
#> 2  0.05922709  0.2442293      2  0.18484918  0.4772373
#> 3  0.80887279 -0.5117871      3  1.58784533 -0.5965582
#> 4 -0.81997210  0.5303289      4 -1.13037567  0.7922033
#> 5 -0.14375128  0.2680057      5 -0.08025176  0.2896367
#> 6  0.12394223  0.4742975      6  0.13242028  0.7389386
plot(pred_ord[,c(1,2)])


# with newdata
new <- data.frame(temp = c(-1, 0, 1), moist = c(0, 0, 0))
pred_new <- predict(fit, newdata = new)
head(pred_new)
#>   s1 s2      2.5%       50%     97.5%
#> 1  1  2 0.2358371 0.4706934 0.6278474
#> 2  1  3 0.5744552 0.7027264 0.7928866
#> 3  2  3 0.2371924 0.4687820 0.6363789

# Predict position in ordination
pred_new_ord <- predict(fit,
                        newdata = new,
                        ordination = TRUE,
                        n_sim = 500)

# Visualise sample-level variability
plot(pred_new_ord$L.1,
     pred_new_ord$L.2,
     xlab = 'L1',
     ylab = 'L2',
     asp = 1,
     col = c('blue', 'grey', 'red')[as.numeric(as.factor(pred_new_ord$temp))])
